intended_object: The last standard basis vector e_{n+1} = (0,…,0,1) of ℝ^{n+1}, seen as a point of the unit sphere S^n = {x : Σ x_i² = 1}. The sphere is the unit level set of the positive-definite form of signature (n+1, 0). It serves as the basepoint for the orbit map Spin(n+1) → S^n. This comes from the docstring and the module (Spin/Real/Orbit/Bundle).
explanation:
`realCliffordUnitLevel m` is the set {x : Fin m → ℝ | realCliffordForm m 0 x = 1}. Here `realCliffordForm m 0` is the weighted sum of squares with all weights equal to +1, i.e. the standard Euclidean quadratic form. The library also proves this set homeomorphic to the unit sphere in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`, and makes it a sub-action of the spin group Spin(m).

The definition takes `Pi.single (Fin.last n) 1`, which is exactly e_{n+1}. Membership holds because the form takes the value 1 on every standard basis vector, which is the lemma `realCliffordForm_zero_single_one`.

This is one specific point, the north pole, chosen as the basepoint of the orbit map for the fibration Spin(n) → Spin(n+1) → S^n. Being specific does not make it too narrow, and the index shift `n + 1` is what keeps the sphere nonempty. It matches its docstring.
